summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for planned initiation of hemodialysis due to end-stage renal disease from polycystic kidney disease. She reported symptoms of fluid overload including leg swelling, dyspnea on exertion, and abdominal discomfort from enlarged kidneys. She underwent three hemodialysis sessions without complications and showed clinical improvement in volume status and breathing. Medications were adjusted, including discontinuation of atenolol, valsartan, furosemide, darbepoetin, iron, and hectorol, with continuation of amiodarone, coumadin, lisinopril, and amlodipine. A chest X-ray showed no pulmonary congestion. The patient tolerated the transition well, was stable at discharge, and returned home with follow-up arranged. DNR/DNI status was discussed and documented.
problems: Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
